subject: general
question: In △ABC, BD ⟂ AC at D and ∠DBC = 22°. E is a point on BC such that ∠CAE = 36°. What is the measure of ∠AEB?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **ΔBDC**, since **BD ⊥ AC**, **∠C** = 90° − **∠DBC** = 90° − 22° = 68°.

In **ΔAEC**, **∠AEB** is the **exterior angle** at vertex **E** because **B, E, C** are collinear.

By the **Exterior Angle Theorem**, **∠AEB** = **∠CAE** + **∠C**.

⇒ **∠AEB** = 36° + 68° = 104°.

**∴ The correct answer is 104°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** In **ΔABC**, **BD ⊥ AC** at **D**, **∠DBC = 22°**, and **∠CAE = 36°** where **E** is on **BC**.

**Formula Used:** Sum of angles in a triangle = 180°; Linear pair of angles sum to 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/92a773a45eb75167a03a926a5a75ba56d37225184ce2f5a1a86469ac174e22a6.png] 

In **ΔBDC**:

⇒ **∠BDC** = 90° (Since **BD ⊥ AC**)

⇒ **∠BCD** + **∠DBC** + **∠BDC** = 180°

⇒ **∠BCD** + 22° + 90° = 180°

⇒ **∠BCD** = 180° − 112° = 68°

In **ΔAEC**:

⇒ **∠CAE** = 36° (Given)

⇒ **∠ACE** = **∠BCD** = 68°

⇒ **∠AEC** = 180° − (**∠CAE** + **∠ACE**)

⇒ **∠AEC** = 180° − (36° + 68°) = 180° − 104° = 76°

Since **B, E, C** lie on a straight line:

⇒ **∠AEB** + **∠AEC** = 180° (Linear pair)

⇒ **∠AEB** = 180° − 76° = 104°

**∴ The correct answer is 104°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exterior Angle Theorem

The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the measures of its two remote interior angles.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of the interior angles of any triangle is always 180°.

Linear Pair Postulate

If two angles form a linear pair, then the measures of the angles add up to 180°.</p
